columns.name: sequenceReference
columns.description: A reference to a SequenceReference on which the location is defined.

columns.name: loc_start

derivation.transform: the integer start; NULL when start is a Range ([min, max] list)

columns.description: The start coordinate or range of the SequenceLocation. The minimum value of this coordinate or range is 0. For locations on linear sequences, this MUST represent a coordinate or range less than or equal to the value of `end`. For circular sequences, `start` is greater than `end` when the location spans the sequence 0 coordinate.

columns.name: loc_start_min

derivation.transform: COALESCE(integer start, start[0])

columns.description: Lower bound of start: the integer, or the Range's first bound (NULL when open).

columns.name: loc_start_max

derivation.transform: COALESCE(integer start, start[1])

columns.description: Upper bound of start: the integer, or the Range's second bound (NULL when open).

columns.name: loc_end

derivation.transform: the integer end; NULL when end is a Range ([min, max] list)

columns.description: The end coordinate or range of the SequenceLocation. The minimum value of this coordinate or range is 0. For locations on linear sequences, this MUST represent a coordinate or range greater than or equal to the value of `start`. For circular sequences, `end` is less than `start` when the location spans the sequence 0 coordinate.

columns.name: loc_end_min

derivation.transform: COALESCE(integer end, end[0])

columns.description: Lower bound of end: the integer, or the Range's first bound (NULL when open).

columns.name: loc_end_max

derivation.transform: COALESCE(integer end, end[1])

columns.description: Upper bound of end: the integer, or the Range's second bound (NULL when open).

columns.name: membershipOperator
columns.description: The logical relationship between concepts in the set, in the context of some knowledge reported about them. The value 'AND' indicates that the concepts are dependent and occur together in this context - i.e. the reported assertion is not necessarily true for each concept on its own - only in combination with the other(s). The value 'OR' indicates that each concept applies independently in this context - i.e. the reported assertion is necessarily true for each concept on its own, independent of the presence of the other(s).

columns.description: The possible fact against which evidence items contained in an Evidence Line were collectively evaluated, in determining the overall strength and direction of support they provide. For example, in an ACMG Guideline-based assessment of variant pathogenicity, the support provided by distinct lines of evidence are assessed against a target proposition that the variant is pathogenic for a specific disease.

columns.description: A term used to report the strength of a Proposition's assessment in the direction indicated (i.e. how strongly supported or disputed the Proposition is believed to be). Implementers may choose to frame a strength assessment in terms of how *confident* an agent is that the Proposition is true or false, or in terms of the *strength of all evidence* they believe supports or disputes it.

columns.name: quality
columns.description: A term used to report the quality of the assessment of a Proposition taking into consideration the reliability of the method, the contributor's self-reporting of the rigor of the evaluation, and the overall robustness of the supporting or disputing evidence. This is useful when there is a consistent policy and authority that manages and a governing framework for evaluating the quality of evidence. Also known as trust rating, review status or ranking.

columns.name: hasEvidenceLines

derivation.transform: strip ^#/[^/]+/ from each pointer, in order

columns.description: Evidence lines grouping contributing submissions by review status priority tier. Each evidence line contains nested sub-statements (classification layer) or SCV references (aggregate contribution layer). Tiers are: practice guideline (PG), expert panel (EP), criteria provided (CP), no criteria provided (NOCP), no classification provided (NOCL), and flagged submission (FLAG).

columns.name: ordinal
columns.description: The record's position in its bundle section (0 = its first record line).

columns.name: id
columns.description: The bundle key.

columns.name: type
columns.description: MUST be "Statement".

columns.name: direction
columns.description: A term indicating whether the Statement supports, disputes, or remains neutral w.r.t. the validity of the Proposition it evaluates.

columns.name: strength
columns.description: A term used to report the strength of a Proposition's assessment in the direction indicated (i.e. how strongly supported or disputed the Proposition is believed to be). Implementers may choose to frame a strength assessment in terms of how *confident* an agent is that the Proposition is true or false, or in terms of the *strength of all evidence* they believe supports or disputes it.

columns.name: quality
columns.description: A term used to report the quality of the assessment of a Proposition taking into consideration the reliability of the method, the contributor's self-reporting of the rigor of the evaluation, and the overall robustness of the supporting or disputing evidence. This is useful when there is a consistent policy and authority that manages and a governing framework for evaluating the quality of evidence. Also known as trust rating, review status or ranking.

columns.name: classification
columns.type: STRUCT("type" VARCHAR, conceptType VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR, "extensions" STRUCT("name" VARCHAR, value_string VARCHAR)[])

derivation.transform: nested extensions: {name, value} -> {name, value_<kind>} by the JSON kind of value

columns.description: A single term or phrase summarizing the result of direction and strength assessments of a Statement's Proposition, in terms of a classification of its subject.

columns.name: proposition
columns.description: The aggregate proposition assessed by this VCV or RCV statement. Uses the same proposition types as SCV statements. The proposition at the aggregate level represents the consensus or highest-priority classification across contributing submissions.

columns.name: proposition_section

derivation.transform: the <section> of the pointer

columns.description: The section proposition names.
